notes: Faithfully and accurately translates the complete Sanskrit verse introducing the royal secret knowledge without omissions or boundary bleeding.
Faithfully and accurately translates all seven epithets of the sovereign science and sovereign secret without omissions or boundary bleeding.
Faithfully and accurately translates the warning to those lacking faith in this dharma without omissions or boundary bleeding.
Accurately renders verse 9.4 in full, but exhibits forward boundary bleeding by annexing the opening hemistich clause of verse 9.5 ('Nor yet do all entities live in me').
Suffers bidirectional boundary bleeding: lost its opening clause to verse 9.4 and its concluding clause to verse 9.6, leaving an incomplete sentence fragment.
Accurately translates the cosmic simile of verse 9.6 in full, but suffers backward boundary bleeding from the annexed concluding clause of verse 9.5.
Faithfully and accurately translates the cyclic dissolution and cosmic recreation at the end and beginning of a kalpa without omissions or boundary bleeding.
Accurately translates verse 9.8 in full, but exhibits slight forward boundary bleeding by annexing the opening conjunction 'But' of verse 9.9.
Faithfully translates verse 9.9 on divine detachment from action, lacking only the initial conjunction severed and annexed to verse 9.8.
Accurately translates verse 9.10, but exhibits forward boundary bleeding by annexing the subject of verse 9.11 and the initial epithet of verse 9.12 ('Deluded people of vain hopes').
Catastrophic alignment failure: reduced to an isolated two-word fragment ('vain acts' from verse 9.12), while the entire text of 9.11 is scattered into verses 9.10 and 9.13.
Catastrophic alignment failure: reduced to an isolated two-word fragment ('vain knowledge'), with the remainder of the verse scattered across verses 9.10, 9.11, and 9.13.
Severe alignment distortion: heavily contaminated by displaced clauses from verses 9.12 and 9.11, while losing its own concluding predicate clause to verse 9.14.
Suffers bidirectional boundary bleeding: prepended with the predicate clause of verse 9.13 and truncated at the end by the loss of its concluding clause to verse 9.15.
Accurately translates verse 9.15 in full, but suffers backward boundary bleeding from the annexed concluding clause of verse 9.14.
Accurately translates verse 9.16 in full, but exhibits forward boundary bleeding by annexing the opening clause of verse 9.17 ('I am the father of this universe').
Truncated at the boundary by losing its opening clause ('I am the father of this universe') to verse 9.16, though accurately rendering the remaining attributes.
Accurately and completely translates all twelve divine epithets and cosmic attributes of verse 9.18 without omissions or boundary bleeding.
Faithfully and accurately translates the complete Sanskrit verse on cosmic sovereignty over heat, rain, immortality, and being without omissions or boundary bleeding.
Accurately translates verse 9.20 in full, but exhibits forward boundary bleeding by annexing the opening hemistich clause of verse 9.21 ('And having enjoyed that great heavenly world').
Suffers bidirectional boundary bleeding: lacks its opening heavenly enjoyment clause (lost to 9.20) and its concluding transit predicate (lost to 9.22).
Accurately renders verse 9.22 and its promise of yoga-kṣema in full, but suffers backward boundary bleeding from the annexed concluding phrase of verse 9.21.
Truncated at the boundary: preserves only the conditional protasis, while its principal finite clause ('worship me only, (but) irregularly') bled into verse 9.24.
Accurately translates verse 9.24 in full, but suffers backward boundary bleeding from the prepended concluding clause of verse 9.23.
Faithfully and accurately translates the fourfold destinations of divine, ancestral, elemental, and Vishnu worshippers without omissions or boundary bleeding.
Faithfully and accurately translates the celebrated verse on the humble offering of a leaf, flower, fruit, or water without omissions or boundary bleeding.
Faithfully and accurately translates the universal dedication of all actions, eating, oblations, charity, and austerities without omissions or boundary bleeding.
Faithfully and accurately translates the liberation from pleasant and unpleasant karmic fruits through saṃnyāsa-yoga without omissions or boundary bleeding.
Faithfully and accurately translates the verse on divine impartiality and mutual communion with devoted souls without omissions or boundary bleeding.
Faithfully and accurately translates the redemption of even an evil-doer who worships with undivided devotion without omissions or boundary bleeding.

Accurately translates verse 9.31, but exhibits forward boundary bleeding by annexing the opening clause and subject list of verse 9.32 ('For, O son of Pṛthā! even those who are of sinful birth, women, Vaiśyas').
Truncated at the boundary: lost its opening hemistich and initial subjects to verse 9.31, preserving only the concluding clause for Śūdras.
Faithfully and accurately translates the comparison with holy Brahmins and royal sages and the call to worship in this transient world without omissions or boundary bleeding.
Faithfully and accurately translates the culminating verse on wholehearted devotion and supreme attainment without omissions or boundary bleeding.
